page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfr6.4xlarge is an x86_64 compute instance belonging to the high clock speed family, structured with a heavy memory allocation. It features 16 dedicated virtual CPUs derived from 8 physical cores on an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at a base clock speed of 3.1 GHz. The architecture incorporates 35 MB of shared L3 cache and supports instruction sets including AVX-512, VNNI, and AES-NI. The instance is allocated 128 GB of RAM, yielding an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio that categorizes it as a memory-dense environment.

The instance delivers steady throughput across industry standard synthetic tests. In CPU workloads, it achieves a Geekbench single-core score of 1287.0 and a multi-core score of 7935.0, alongside a PassMark CPU score of 16780.3. Memory testing highlights an uncached large-block read bandwidth of 90.41 GB/sec and an uncached write bandwidth of 49.06 GB/sec. Application-oriented tests record Redis throughput reaching 14.91 million operations per second and static web serving capacity of 12.32 GB/sec. Prompt processing for small 135M parameter language models reaches 937.39 tokens per second, though medium 7B model prompt processing drops into the lower quartile at 23.2 tokens per second.

Hardware tradeoffs for the ecs.hfr6.4xlarge include the absence of dedicated local storage, requiring attached network volumes for persistent storage. GPU hardware acceleration is not present. Network performance is anchored at a baseline bandwidth of 5 Gbps. Given its 128 GB memory allotment paired with 16 dedicated threads, this instance demonstrates balanced resource density for in-memory databases, memory-constrained data manipulation pipelines, backend web tiers, and caching systems.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfr6.4xlarge is a high-clock-speed, memory-dense virtual machine powered by an Intel Xeon 8269CY x86_64 processor clocked at 3.1 GHz. Configured with 16 dedicated vCPUs (8 physical cores) and 128 GB of RAM, it maintains an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. Architectural extensions include AVX-512 and AES-NI, backed by 35 MB of L3 cache. Benchmark evaluations demonstrate solid baseline throughput, including a PassMark CPU score of 16780.3, uncached memory read bandwidth of 90.41 GB/sec, and 14.91 million Redis SET operations per second. The instance provides a baseline network throughput of 5 Gbps and contains no bundled local storage or GPUs. It is technically suited for in-memory caching layers, Redis instances, relational databases, and enterprise application backends requiring stable dedicated CPU frequency and substantial memory overhead.
